text:
andrew: quick idea - we should add a focused pause/unpause API + console control for config rollouts (feature switches, routing predicates). basically a kill-switch for a specific config id so oncall can stop a rollout without reverting the config + without a full deploy.
jenna: +1. this has come up a few times during weird quota spikes. what's the proposed behaviour for traffic? 503 vs fallback model vs degraded path?
mike: my vote is route to fallback variant if available (same as existing fallback routing). 503 will panic lots of callers. fallback lets apps fail more gracefully.
claudia: agree with routing to fallback. also require an audit entry and reason text so we can correlate to an incident id.
andrew: prototype API shape:
```
POST /v1/configs/:config_id/pause
{ "actor": "andrew", "reason": "incident/1234", "ttl_seconds": 900 }

response 200:
{ "config_id": "cfg-xyz", "paused": true, "expires_at": "2026-04-01T12:34:56Z", "actor": "andrew" }
```
jenna: make TTL optional with sensible default (15m) and require an explicit unpause. also add a short lived capability token so scripts can call it without long-lived perms.
olivia: console UX idea: small "Pause rollout" button next to the rollout slider. click -> modal with reason + TTL dropdown + checkbox "attach to incident". show who paused and remaining TTL on the config tile. :eyes:
mike: concurrency question - how do we avoid races if someone toggles rollout at the same time? optimistic eTag? server-side last-write-wins is scary.
claudia: eTag + config version compare. Pause should be a separate object tied to config_id, not a change to the config blob itself. avoids merge conflicts.
andrew: good point. implement pause as separate resource /v1/configs/:id/pause-records/:pause_id. pause activation should be atomic in router: check pause table before evaluating routing predicates.
sre-bot: alert rule proposal: create metric "config_pause_count" + event log stream. trigger if pause on >3 configs in 5m from non-sre principal -> page ops.
ops-runbooks: please add pause/unpause steps to runbooks. when paused, operators should run a quick impact check and either unpause or start rollback depending on metrics.
jenna: telemetry - instrument a flag "pauses.active" per config and emit reason tag. dashboards should graph pause events next to error/latency deltas for easier RCA.
claudia: question: auto-unpause? i'm wary. maybe support auto-expire (TTL) but default is manual unpause. auto-unpause should require a different permission (since it can reopen a bad rollout).
andrew: agree. default: TTL allowed, but manual unpause recommended. also add optional pre-and-post snapshots: capture counters just before pause and 5m after for quick lookup.
mike: permission model: IAM:configs.pause and IAM:configs.unpause. UI hides button if no permission.
olivia: UX detail: when paused, show an inline banner on the console route page with time left and "unpause" button + audit link.
jenna: API auth: require identity header X-Request-Principal. log the principal in audit and events.
claudia: one more: what happens for private/dedicated customers? should pause be tenant-scoped and operator-scoped? probably yes - a customer-admin pause should only affect their traffic, not global routing policies.
andrew: yes tenant-scoped. for Dedicated we also need to surface pause to infra team so we can adjust capacity alarms. add a webhook callback for pause events per tenant.
ops-runbooks: include recommended quick checks: 1) slow logs 2) tail error rates 3) quota burn rate 4) fallback routing success rate. if fallback failing, proceed to rollback.
jenna: timeline: spike-free prototype: API + minimal console button + eTag + audit + TTL by EOW. SRE/release to canary for a week.
andrew: i'll spin up a PR for the API and basic console button. will add a short runbook doc and link the webhook.
olivia: I'll mock up modal and banner today, drop screenshots in the PR. :thumbsup:
mike: +1. happy to review concurrency bits.
claudia: +1 from infra side. will own webhook + webhook auth.
andrew: ok thanks team. will ping ops-runbooks and @sre-bot for alerts hookup once PR is ready.
